item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is substantially closer to the frozen contract and is the patch I would review and merge, though it should be adjusted so Upload calls Add directly and Add retains its prior behavior.","reasons":["B adds only the requested Upload API, uses internal/multipartbody.NewFile with field \"file\", and keeps the change focused.","B’s Upload body is replayable through the returned bytes.Reader, and its retry test verifies field name, filename, content, and two complete attempts after a 429.","A explicitly violates scope constraints by adding association fields/options, NewFileWithFields, and broad RawClient request-body/retry machinery.","A’s Upload bypasses FilesService.Add and duplicates Add’s option handling, request construction, decoding, and missing-data behavior, contrary to the required routing through Add."],"risks_a":["Adds forbidden association APIs and changes FilesOption-related machinery.","Refactors unrelated retry and body-closing semantics across Raw.Do and other upload paths.","Introduces substantial duplicate request logic in Upload instead of reusing Add as required."],"risks_b":["Add now buffers every caller-encoded body, changing its existing streaming behavior; the contract requires preserving Add.","Upload calls a new private add helper instead of routing through the public Add method as explicitly required.","The visible tests do not cover empty filename, nil content, or source-reader errors, and the original Add test was replaced rather than retained."]}
